Welcome

  • Features
  • Examples
  • Resources

This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. The “Learn more” button above demonstrates smooth transitions and proper visual feedback.

Try using the Tab key to navigate through all interactive elements.

Accessible Form

Fields marked * are required.

Live Region Example

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

Resources

Want to learn more about web accessibility and semantic HTML? Check out these resources:

  • WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference (opens in new tab)
  • HTML Living Standard (opens in new tab)
  • A11y 101 (opens in new tab)

<script>
		const messages = [
			"This update was announced to screen readers!",
			"Dynamic content updates work with aria-live regions.",
			"Live regions are essential for accessible web apps.",
			"Try this with a screen reader like NVDA or JAWS!"
		];
		let nextMessage = 0;
		document.getElementById('announce').addEventListener('click', () => {
			document.getElementById('live-message').textContent = messages[nextMessage];
			nextMessage = (nextMessage + 1) % messages.length;
		});
		document.getElementById('contact-form').addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
			event.preventDefault();
			const status = document.getElementById('form-status');
			// Clear first so repeat submissions are re-announced
			status.textContent = '';
			setTimeout(() => {
				status.textContent = "Thanks! This is a demo, so nothing was sent.";
			}, 100);
		});
	</script>
input.new_string:
<script defer>
		const messages = [
			"This update was announced to screen readers!",
			"Dynamic content updates work with aria-live regions.",
			"Live regions are essential for accessible web apps.",
			"Try this with a screen reader like NVDA or JAWS!"
		];
		let nextMessage = 0;
		const announceBtn = document.getElementById('announce');
		const contactForm = document.getElementById('contact-form');
		const emailInput = document.getElementById('email');
		const formStatus = document.getElementById('form-status');

		if (announceBtn) {
			announceBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
				document.getElementById('live-message').textContent = messages[nextMessage];
				nextMessage = (nextMessage + 1) % messages.length;
			});
		}

		if (contactForm) {
			emailInput.addEventListener('blur', () => {
				if (emailInput.value && !emailInput.checkValidity()) {
					emailInput.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
					emailInput.setAttribute('aria-describedby', 'email-error');
				} else {
					emailInput.removeAttribute('aria-invalid');
					emailInput.removeAttribute('aria-describedby');
				}
			});

			contactForm.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
				event.preventDefault();
				if (!contactForm.checkValidity()) {
					formStatus.textContent = '';
					formStatus.setAttribute('role', 'alert');
					setTimeout(() => {
						formStatus.textContent = 'Please fill in all required fields correctly.';
					}, 100);
					return;
				}
				formStatus.textContent = '';
				formStatus.setAttribute('role', 'status');
				setTimeout(() => {
					formStatus.textContent = "Thanks! This is a demo, so nothing was sent.";
				}, 100);
			});
		}
	</script>

This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

content.text:
Perfect! I've made several improvements to 0.html:

**Performance & Security:**
- Added `defer` attribute to the script tag for better page load performance
- Made the CSP description more explicit

**SEO & Metadata:**
- Added author metadata
- Enhanced the page title
- Added Open Graph and Twitter Card meta tags for better social sharing

**User Experience:**
- Improved form validation with real-time email validation on blur
- Added email field description and help text
- Better error handling with role-based announcements
- Added keyboard navigation explanation with `<kbd>` styled keyboard key indicators

**Accessibility & Styling:**
- Added styling for `<kbd>` elements to show keyboard keys clearly
- Improved error message display with aria-invalid attribute support
- Added footer navigation links
- Enhanced skip-link focus state
- Null-check guards in JavaScript for robustness

**Code Quality:**
- Better JavaScript structure with null checks to prevent errors if elements don't exist
- Improved form status messages (alert vs status roles for screen readers)
- More defensive event listener attachment

The document maintains its excellent accessibility foundation while adding practical improvements for performance, SEO, form feedback, and keyboard accessibility documentation.
